items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this for a premium documentary YouTube Shorts channel about money, history and the tricks behind them. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller with a hint of mystery: curious, quietly amused, energetic and punchy, never slow, never announcer-like. Natural emphasis on dates and numbers, questions end with a curious lift, a short comic pause before each punchline. Keep the same voice, pace and energy from start to finish.
lines: Narrator
Your price tag never moved, but you could be paying twelve percent more. How did your brain miss it?
Narrator
Last year, Milka in Germany went from a hundred grams to ninety. Same wrapper.
Narrator
Only one tiny number changed. It's called shrinkflation.
Narrator
It works because of how you shop.
Narrator
Raise a price one percent, and sales drop about one point two percent. Shrink the pack one percent: only half that.
Narrator
You watch the price. Almost nobody watches the grams.
Narrator
So brands shrink. In US stores, after a downsize, the price per unit rose about twelve percent.
Narrator
In twenty sixteen, Toblerone widened the gaps between its peaks. Fewer mountains, same price.
Narrator
In May, a German court said Milka misled shoppers.
Narrator
That's the mirage: prices don't only rise on the tag. They rise inside the pack.
Narrator
So skip the big number. Check the price per kilo.
Narrator
The sneakiest price rise looks exactly the same.
Narrator
This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
